title: Truthiness of 0
explanation: Only nil and false are falsy in Ruby. 0, "" and [] are all truthy, unlike Python or JavaScript.

title: Array.new with a default object
explanation:
All three slots share one [] object:

a = Array.new(3, [])  # [[], [], []] — same object in every slot
a[0] << 1             # mutates that one array
# a is now [[1], [1], [1]]

Use Array.new(3) { [] } for a fresh array per slot.

title: Symbol and string keys
explanation:
"name" and :name are different keys.
 Hash#[] returns nil for a missing key.
 Hash#fetch would raise KeyError.

title: ||= on false
code:
enabled = false
enabled ||= true
p enabled
explanation: a ||= b assigns when a is falsy, and false is falsy. That makes ||= the wrong tool for defaulting a boolean that may legitimately be false.

title: return inside a block
code:
def find_big
  [1, 2, 3].each { |x| return x * 10 if x == 2 }
  :none
end
p find_big
explanation:
return inside a block returns from the enclosing method, not just from the block.

So when x == 2, return x * 10 exits find_big immediately with 20 
 the :none line is never reached.

title: << mutates a shared string
code:
a = "hi"
b = a
b << "!"
p a
explanation: a and b refer to the same String, and << appends in place. b += "!" would build a new string and leave a as "hi".

title: Integer division
explanation:
Dividing two Integers gives an Integer, rounded toward negative infinity.
 Make one side a Float (7 / 2.0 or 7.fdiv(2)) to get 3.5.

title: Spot the local variable
prompt: Which line assigns a local variable?
code:
1  $flag = true
2  class Box
3    @label = "x"
4    def pack
5      size = 1
6      @size = size
7    end
8  end
explanation: size on line 5 is a local. $flag is global, @label on the class body is a class instance variable, and @size is an instance variable of each Box.

title: Spot the instance variable
prompt: Which line assigns an instance variable of each object?
code:
1  class Box
2    @@n = 0
3    def initialize(name)
4      @name = name
5      tag = :ok
6    end
7  end
explanation: @name on line 4 lives on each Box instance. @@n is a class variable. name on line 3 is a local (the parameter), and tag is a local.

title: Spot the class variable
prompt: Which line assigns a class variable?
code:
1  class Box
2    @@n = 0
3    @n = 0
4    def reset
5      @n = 0
6    end
7  end
explanation: @@n is the class variable. @n on line 3 is a class instance variable (on Box itself). @n on line 5 is an instance variable of each Box object.

title: Spot the class instance variable
prompt: Which line assigns a class instance variable?
code:
1  class Box
2    @@n = 0
3    @n = 0
4    def reset
5      @n = 0
6    end
7  end
explanation: @n in the class body (line 3) sits on the Box object, not on instances. @@n is shared class state. @n inside reset belongs to each instance.

title: Spot the global variable
prompt: Which line assigns a global variable?
explanation: $count is global. count on line 1 is a local. @count on line 4 is a class instance variable of App.

title: Spot the symbol
explanation: :ada is a Symbol. "Ada" is a String. $key is a global, @key an instance variable (of main at top level).

title: Parameters are locals
prompt: Which line introduces the local variable `name`?
code:
1  $name = "x"
2  class User
3    def initialize(name)
4      @name = name
5    end
6  end
explanation: A method parameter is a local. Line 3 introduces name. Line 4 reads that local into @name. $name is a different, global name.

title: Symbol as a hash key
explanation: :id on line 2 is a Symbol. Line 1 uses the string "id". Line 3's id is a local Integer, and line 4 uses that integer as the key.

title: Reading a global
prompt: Which line reads a global variable?
code:
1  def debug
2    out = []
3    out << $stderr
4    out << @log
5  end
explanation: $stderr is a global. out is a local. @log is an instance variable.

title: Class variables and subclasses
prompt: Which line is shared with subclasses?
code:
1  class Animal
2    @@legs = 4
3    @kind = "x"
4  end
5  class Dog < Animal
6    def kind
7      @kind
8    end
9  end
explanation: @@legs is one variable for Animal and Dog together. @kind on line 3 lives only on Animal. @kind on line 7 is Dog's instance variable, a third name.
